clue.text: Complain more flesh visible? That's a warning

blocks.note: to object is to complain or protest
with more skin showing you have less clothing on, read as LESS ON

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about revealing outfits, and a moralist calls it a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cryptic reading: more flesh on view means less on. An OBJECT LESSON is a practical example that teaches by warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a cautionary example from which others should learn, so it serves as a warning.

clue.text: Novel I bought full of principally malicious gossip

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the following letters take a new arrangement
principally means chiefly, pointing to the first letter of the next word
the rearranged letters are full of, so they surround, the selected letter

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A reader's purchase is a book packed with spiteful tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like the book that was bought; it is the signal to rearrange. Gossip here is the person, not the talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigmouth is someone who talks indiscreetly and spreads secrets, a gossip in the sense of a person.

clue.text: Show every last bit of income tax, and weep too

indicators.note: the last bit of every word means the final letter of each in turn

blocks.note: last letter
last letter
last letter
last letter

explanation.surface: Reveal every penny of income tax paid, and cry about it too.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' is not one of the source words; only the four words around it lend their final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is an exhibition or trade fair, a show of goods or ideas.

clue.text: Infant shifting a toy lower down, initially

indicators.note: shifting things move them about, so the letters change their order
initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word before is kept

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A baby moving a plaything further down.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-year-old is a toddler, a very young child, which is what infant broadly means.

clue.text: One who invented no end should be elevated

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the letters means they read upwards, back to front

blocks.note: taken as written
an end of a playing field is a side, as when teams change ends

explanation.surface: An endless inventor deserves to be raised up.
explanation.walkthrough: One who invented no end reads as a prolific inventor, but the definition stops at invented. Thomas Edison invented the phonograph and a practical light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and the commercial electric light bulb.

clue.text: Particular drinks containing something cold, served up

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one word surrounds the other
in a down entry, served up means presented upwards, so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: Fussy about drinks being served with ice in them.
explanation.walkthrough: Particular suggests a fussy drinker; here it is the adjective meaning specific.
explanation.definitionFit: Special and particular both mean distinct from others or specific to one case.

clue.text: Britain's outstanding figure perhaps beaten in battle, and inspiring love

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked about, so the following words are mixed up
inspiring literally means breathing in, so these letters take in the next one

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A great British hero, perhaps, defeated in war yet inspiring devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Outstanding figure reads as an eminent person; it is an unpaid sum, a figure that is outstanding. Beaten in battle looks like a phrase but only beaten is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A national debt is the total money a government owes, an amount still outstanding; perhaps marks Britain's as one example.

clue.text: Land in old money?

blocks.note: first meaning: a country in West Africa
second meaning: a pre-decimal British gold coin worth 21 shillings

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a question about inherited wealth in land; the guinea coin was named after the West African region whose gold minted it.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinea is a West African country, and the guinea was a British coin worth one pound one shilling.

clue.text: Lob and back-hander passed?

blocks.note: first meaning: to throw or toss casually
second meaning: a bribe slipped to someone, British slang

explanation.surface: A tennis commentary: a lob, then a backhand that gets past the opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: Back-hander looks like a tennis shot but is British slang for a bribe, as is BUNG; to bung something is also to chuck it.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a bung is an illicit payment handed over, and to bung is to toss something carelessly.

clue.text: Supporting colliery, leaders in next town striking

indicators.note: leaders are the front-runners, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
a colliery is a coal mine
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Backing the pit while the bosses lead the town out on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: Striking suggests an industrial dispute beside colliery, but it is the adjective meaning eye-catching.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prominent stands out conspicuously, which is what striking also describes.

clue.text: Heavyweight parting long hair, lurid colour

indicators.note: a parting divides hair down the middle, so one word splits the other in two

blocks.note: a shock is a thick, untidy mass of hair
a kingpin is the most important person in a group

explanation.surface: A burly boxer with a long, garishly dyed mane parted in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavyweight suggests a boxer but means a person of influence; parting is apt for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking pink is a vivid, intense shade of pink, the kind of loud colour called lurid.

clue.text: Reportedly large cab

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: handsome can mean large, as in a handsome sum

explanation.surface: Word has it that the taxi is a big one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom was a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, the forerunner of the taxi cab.

clue.text: New price on old cheese

indicators.note: a new version is a fresh arrangement, so the letters that follow are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A shop has repriced its mature cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecorino is a hard Italian cheese made from ewe's milk, one example of the category.

clue.text: Bird finding veldt with route that's circuitous

indicators.note: a circuitous path winds about, so the letters are taken in a roundabout order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird crossing the South African grassland by a winding path.
explanation.walkthrough: With joins the two words being rearranged; veldt is the open grassland of southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The turtle dove is a small migratory dove of Europe and Africa, a species of bird.

clue.text: Main force burst gas out: that's in character

indicators.note: something that bursts is blown apart, so the letters scatter into a new order
the shuffled letters are placed inside the word that comes next

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
a card is an eccentric or amusing character

explanation.surface: A gas main bursts and the main emergency force is out in character.
explanation.walkthrough: Main is the old poetic word for the sea, so a main force is one that guards the seas and shores.
explanation.definitionFit: The coastguard is the service that patrols the sea near the shore, a force of the main or ocean.

clue.text: A brownie running around, irritating little thing

indicators.note: running around turns back on itself, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
a brownie is a household sprite of folklore

explanation.surface: A young Brownie Guide racing about, a little nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownie suggests the junior Girl Guides; here it is the helpful goblin of Scottish folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a tiny biting insect that makes the skin itch, a small source of irritation.

clue.text: Someone unwelcome at home, more loyal about daughter

indicators.note: about means around, so the preceding word wraps round the next

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
truer is the comparative of true, faithful
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An unwanted guest in the house, more faithful to the daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder is a person who enters where they are not wanted, an unwelcome presence.

clue.text: Little bit after theta?

blocks.note: first meaning: a very small amount
second meaning: the Greek letter that follows theta in the alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second definition is by example: the Greek alphabet runs eta, theta, then the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth Greek letter and, being the smallest, gives English its word for a tiny quantity.

clue.text: North American city covered by visitor on tour

indicators.note: covered by means concealed under, so the answer lies within the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: A city that a travelling tourist takes in.
explanation.walkthrough: Covered by suggests a city a traveller covers on a trip; it signals the letters concealed in visiTOR ON TOur.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada, the capital of Ontario.

clue.text: A swimmer in game doing the backstroke? That's a battle!

indicators.note: a backstroke swimmer travels on the back, so the word goes back to front
the preceding words sit inside the word for a game

blocks.note: darts is a pub game
taken as written
a ling is a fish related to the cod

explanation.surface: A swimmer doing backstroke during a game, hailed as a real battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Swimmer is a crossword fish, not a person; the backstroke applies to the game, which then holds the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalingrad was the decisive Second World War siege on the Volga between Germany and the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Deny judge employment

blocks.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a game
use as a noun means employment, as in putting to use

explanation.surface: A judge turns down a job application.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse a request is to deny it, both meaning to decline to grant.

clue.text: Undercover team briefly infiltrating group

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped
infiltrating means getting inside, so these letters go within the next word

blocks.note: a sect is a religious or political group
a crew is a team of workers

explanation.surface: A squad of spies working undercover to infiltrate a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Undercover operations are carried out in secret, hidden from those being watched.

clue.text: Tale ultimately penned by old actress — might she work on the plot?

definitions.text: might she work on the plot?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter is taken
something penned is shut in a pen, so it goes inside the name that follows

blocks.note: Ava Gardner, the Hollywood star of the 1940s and 50s
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A story written by a veteran actress, who might be good with a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Plot sounds like the storyline of a tale; the definition reads it as a patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener tends a garden, and a plot is a small piece of land for growing things.

clue.text: Fear cracks in lead — very basic construction

indicators.note: something that cracks breaks up, so its letters fall into a new order
the broken-up letters go inside the next element

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: Worry that a leaden roof is cracking in a flimsy building.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a house made of factory-built parts put together on site, a simple and utilitarian building.

clue.text: Ear on table is corn, primarily

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, relating to the ear

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of the words count

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: An ear of corn lying on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Ear plus corn suggests an ear of corn, but ear is the definition; the answer is a medical adjective, so the fit is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the anatomical adjective for the ear, as in otic drops.

clue.text: Corrected mentors in private

indicators.note: a corrected text has been put right by rearranging it, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Tutors put right behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: In looks like part of the phrase in private, but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Innermost thoughts are the most intimate and personal ones, kept private from others.

clue.text: Lovely item of crockery

blocks.note: first meaning: an attractive person, a lovely
second meaning: a plate or bowl for food

explanation.walkthrough: Lovely reads as an adjective praising the crockery, but it is the noun, a lovely, meaning a good-looking person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is informal for a very attractive person, and also a shallow container for serving food.

clue.text: Understand what's what — as might professional musician?

blocks.note: first meaning: to be aware of the real situation
second meaning, taken literally: to be familiar with the written music

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that the idiom is read literally for the second meaning: a player who knows the written music.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to grasp the facts of a situation; a score is also the printed music an orchestra plays from.
